trigger: Unauthorized access of electronic personal information of Florida residents: name with SSN, passport or driver license number, account number with an access code or password, medical information, or health insurance ID; or a username or email with its password. Clock starts at determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination; a 15-day extension for good cause applies only to this notice, if good cause for delay is given in writing to the Department within the 30 days
notify: Each affected Florida resident by mail or email (family members, household and office employees)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - covered entity. The Safeguards Rule has no individual notice duty, so the 501.171(4)(g) federal-regulator safe harbor does not help here

trigger: After an appropriate investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the office reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Written determination kept at least 5 years; provided to the Department within 30 days after the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the office relies on it

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination (no extension for this notice)
applies_at_this_tier: Not expected - the office holds personal information on fewer than 100 people; keep for completeness

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
applies_at_this_tier: No - fewer than 1,000 individuals

trigger: A law enforcement agency determines individual notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay on the agency's written request for the period it specifies
notify: Hold Florida individual notices; keep the written request
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if requested

obligation: Office as third-party agent: notice to a subsidiary (outbound)
trigger: Breach of an office system holding personal information the office maintains for a subsidiary
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after determination (office policy: 24 hours, POL-03 4.9)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if subsidiary personal information is involved

obligation: Vendor as third-party agent: notice to the office (inbound)
trigger: Breach of a system maintained by a vendor for the office (MSP, bill pay, payroll, vault, investment platform)
deadline: No later than 10 days after the vendor's determination
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - add to vendor contracts at renewal

trigger: Affected individuals who reside outside Florida (one adult child and that household; any former household employee who moved)
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Residents and regulators under each state's law
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - check residency of every affected person

obligation: FTC notice of a notification event
trigger: Unauthorized acquisition of unencrypted customer information of at least 500 consumers (unauthorized access is presumed to be acquisition unless reliable evidence shows otherwise). Discovery is the first day any employee, officer, or agent other than the person committing the breach knows
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 30 days after discovery; electronic form on the FTC website
applies_at_this_tier: Applies, but not reachable at current size: the office holds customer information on 11 individuals

obligation: Bank and custodian fraud notice and recall request
trigger: Suspected fraudulent wire or ACH, compromised approver credentials, or a changed payee
deadline: Immediately; recall chances fall within hours
notify: Sending bank's fraud line; custodians' service desks; bill pay vendor
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal

trigger: Payment fraud, business email compromise, or extortion
deadline: As soon as possible after calling the bank
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - voluntary; also a mitigating factor for OFAC if a ransom is ever considered

trigger: Suspected security incident, payment fraud, extortion demand, or data theft
deadline: Per policy: prompt notice through the breach hotline before hiring outside firms; social engineering fraud coverage requires documented verification of payment changes
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal

citation: Management agreements (security terms to be added; R-018)
trigger: Incident affecting the Subsidiaries site, a subsidiary's payments, or subsidiary guest accounts
deadline: Within 24 hours (office policy, POL-03 4.9)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - policy now; contractual from 2027

trigger: Incident affecting a family member's information or accounts
deadline: Same day for account takeover or payment fraud; with or before any legal notice otherwise
notify: Affected family members; the Principal informs the Board of Managers
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - policy

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransom or extortion payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement (FBI) or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI through IC3 or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons

trigger: Material cybersecurity incident at an SEC registrant
deadline: Within 4 business days after determining materiality
applies_at_this_tier: No - the office is not an SEC registrant (N55-R02)

trigger: Notification incident at a bank holding company or savings and loan holding company
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 36 hours after determining a notification incident occurred
notify: Federal Reserve Board-designated point of contact
applies_at_this_tier: No - the office controls no bank (N55-R04)

trigger: Breach of unsecured PHI held by or for the group health plan
deadline: Per HIPAA (the insurer handles notices for PHI it holds)
applies_at_this_tier: No - the office receives only enrollment information; family medical bills are personal information under Florida law, not PHI (N55-R06)

obligation: CIRCIA incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after a ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25 (voluntary until then); recheck when final (N55-R07)

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or services
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification; further report within 10 business days
applies_at_this_tier: No - the office holds no federal contracts

trigger: Contractor identifies a covered article
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification; further report within 10 business days
applies_at_this_tier: No - the office holds no federal contracts
